worksheet.title: Which One Does Not Belong?
worksheet.subtitle: Finding the odd one out
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the one that does not belong with the others.

parts.title: One does not belong
parts.text: Most of these are the same. One is different. Help Bit find the one that does NOT belong, and circle it.

parts.title: Watch Bit — three circles and one triangle
parts.note: Three are circles. The triangle ▲ does not belong — it is the odd one out.

parts.title: Circle the odd one out
parts.prompt: Three are the same. Circle the one that does not belong.

parts.title: Circle the odd one out
parts.prompt: Three are the same. Circle the one that does not belong.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Find the one that does not belong and circle it.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: To find the odd one out, you decide what matters — here it is the shape. Choosing what matters is called abstraction. Computers do it too, to spot what is different.

teacher_guide.title: Which One Does Not Belong?
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 5. Which One Does Not Belong? — Teacher Guide

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children find the one shape in a group that does not match the others. Deciding what matters and ignoring the rest is a first thinking-skill behind coding — it is how computers spot what is different. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child circles the odd one out. Optional: a tray of objects where one does not belong, to find by hand first.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Point to circle, circle, circle, triangle: "three are circles — which one is different?" Circle the triangle.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — three stars and one circle; circle the circle.
3. Let them try. Children do Exercise 2, then Exercise 3 on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — star, star, circle, star → circle the circle. Exercise 2 — square, triangle, square, square → circle the triangle.
Exercise 3 — circle, circle, star, circle, circle → circle the star.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: circling a shape just because it is at the end. Ask "how is it different?"
Make it easier: start with two same + one different before four-card groups.
Make it harder: ask the child to say WHY it does not belong (it is a triangle, the rest are circles).
Make it active: stand in a small group where one child holds a different card — who does not belong?

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children classify objects and notice which one does not belong.
In plain terms: noticing the one thing that does not fit the group.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child circles the single odd shape in each group and can say what makes the others the same.
